$comment: Promissory note and loan agreement. Jurisdiction-neutral drafting only: interest caps, collection rules, and enforcement mechanics differ everywhere, so anywhere a number is a legal judgement it is a [bracketed blank] and the rationale says why. Nothing here asserts what any law requires. The note is the short signed promise; the loan agreement is the fuller two-party contract around it.

clauses.title: Promise to Pay
clauses.rationale: The operative sentence of the entire document — everything else qualifies it.
clauses.body: For value received, {{borrowerName}} (“Borrower”) promises to pay {{company}} (“Lender”) the principal sum of {{principalAmount}}, on the terms of this Promissory Note dated {{date}}.

clauses.title: Interest
clauses.rationale: Included when the wizard names a rate. Interest caps differ from place to place, and a rate above the local cap can undermine the whole loan — checking the rate is part of adapting this document to where the parties are.
clauses.body: The unpaid principal bears interest at {{interestText}}, computed from the date Lender advances the funds until the principal is paid in full. Interest accrues on the basis of a [365]-day year for the actual number of days elapsed.

clauses.title: Interest
clauses.rationale: Saying “no interest” expressly beats silence — silence invites the argument that some rate was implied. Interest-free loans between related parties can have tax consequences worth asking a professional about; the document does not attempt to address them.
clauses.body: This Promissory Note is interest-free: the unpaid principal bears no interest.

clauses.title: Repayment
clauses.rationale: The installment variant. The payment amount is left blank rather than computed: computing it correctly requires an amortization decision the user has not been asked to make.
clauses.body: Borrower will repay in equal monthly installments of [amount] on the [1st] day of each month, beginning on [first payment date] and continuing until the principal and any accrued interest are paid in full. The final payment is the entire remaining balance.

clauses.title: Repayment
clauses.rationale: The single-payment variant — one date, one amount, no schedule to administer.
clauses.body: Borrower will repay the entire principal and any accrued interest in a single payment on [maturity date].

clauses.title: Repayment
clauses.rationale: The on-demand variant. A notice period is included so “demand” has a defined runway instead of meaning “this afternoon”.
clauses.body: The entire principal and any accrued interest are payable upon Lender’s written demand, delivered to Borrower at least [10] days before the payment date the demand names.

clauses.title: How Payments Are Made and Applied
clauses.rationale: The application order (costs, then interest, then principal) is the convention lenders expect; making it express avoids the argument later.
clauses.body: Borrower will make payments to Lender at [address or account Lender designates in writing]. Payments are applied first to any costs owed under this Promissory Note, then to accrued interest, then to principal.

clauses.title: Prepayment
clauses.rationale: Personal and small-business notes almost always allow free prepayment; a lender who wants a prepayment charge should be making that choice deliberately, so the default here is penalty-free.
clauses.body: Borrower may prepay all or part of the principal at any time without penalty. Prepayments are applied to principal and do not postpone any scheduled payment unless Lender agrees in writing.

clauses.title: Default and Acceleration
clauses.rationale: Notice-and-cure before acceleration is the fair-dealing default; a lender who wants hair-trigger acceleration should have to edit this on the page and see what they are doing.
clauses.body: If Borrower misses a payment and does not cure within [10] days after Lender’s written notice of the missed payment, Borrower is in default, and Lender may declare the entire unpaid principal and accrued interest immediately due. Lender’s decision not to accelerate after one default does not give up the right to accelerate after another.

clauses.title: Collection Costs
clauses.rationale: Offered rather than automatic: fee-shifting is a real economic choice, and some places read one-way fee clauses as two-way.
clauses.body: If Borrower defaults, Borrower will pay Lender’s reasonable costs of collection, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, to the extent the parties may lawfully agree to them where enforcement occurs.

clauses.title: Security
clauses.rationale: Included when the wizard says the loan is secured. Making a security interest enforceable against third parties usually takes steps beyond this sentence (describing the collateral precisely, and often a filing) — the rationale flags it because the document cannot do it for you.
clauses.body: This Promissory Note is secured by the following property of Borrower: [describe the collateral precisely — e.g. the 2021 pickup truck, VIN …]. The parties’ agreement about that collateral is set out in the Loan Agreement of the same date.

clauses.title: Security
clauses.rationale: Saying “unsecured” expressly stops the later argument that some pledge was implied in conversation.
clauses.body: This Promissory Note is unsecured. No property of Borrower secures it.

clauses.title: Parties and Purpose
clauses.rationale: Frames the fuller agreement around the note: same parties, same money, more machinery.
clauses.body: This Loan Agreement is entered into as of {{date}} between {{company}} (“Lender”) and {{borrowerName}} (“Borrower”). Lender agrees to lend and Borrower agrees to borrow the principal sum of {{principalAmount}} (the “Loan”) on the terms below.

clauses.title: Disbursement
clauses.rationale: When and how the money actually moves — the term people forget until the wire has not arrived.
clauses.body: Lender will advance the Loan to Borrower on or before [date], by [method — e.g. bank transfer to the account Borrower designates in writing]. Lender’s obligation to advance ends if Borrower is in default of this Loan Agreement before the advance is made.

clauses.title: Promissory Note
clauses.rationale: Ties the two documents in the package together and says which controls if they ever disagree.
clauses.body: Borrower’s repayment obligation is also evidenced by a Promissory Note of the same date in the principal amount of {{principalAmount}}. If this Loan Agreement and the Promissory Note conflict, this Loan Agreement controls.

clauses.title: Interest
clauses.rationale: Mirrors the note. Interest caps differ from place to place; checking the rate locally is part of adapting the documents.
clauses.body: The unpaid principal bears interest at {{interestText}}, from the date the Loan is advanced until repaid in full, computed on a [365]-day year for actual days elapsed.

clauses.title: Interest
clauses.rationale: Mirrors the note: express interest-free beats silence.
clauses.body: The Loan is interest-free: the unpaid principal bears no interest.

clauses.title: Repayment
clauses.rationale: Mirrors the note’s installment variant so the two documents cannot drift apart on schedule.
clauses.body: Borrower will repay in equal monthly installments of [amount] on the [1st] day of each month, beginning on [first payment date], until the principal and any accrued interest are paid in full. The final payment is the entire remaining balance.

clauses.title: Repayment
clauses.rationale: Mirrors the note’s single-payment variant.
clauses.body: Borrower will repay the entire principal and any accrued interest in a single payment on [maturity date].

clauses.title: Repayment
clauses.rationale: Mirrors the note’s on-demand variant, with the same defined runway.
clauses.body: The entire principal and any accrued interest are payable upon Lender’s written demand, delivered to Borrower at least [10] days before the payment date the demand names.

clauses.title: Prepayment
clauses.rationale: Offered in the agreement (it is automatic in the note) so the user notices if they are creating a mismatch between the two documents.
clauses.body: Borrower may prepay all or part of the principal at any time without penalty. Prepayments are applied to principal and do not postpone any scheduled payment unless Lender agrees in writing.

clauses.title: Use of the Loan
clauses.rationale: Offered for lenders who care what the money is for — common in family and small-business lending, meaningless in others.
clauses.body: Borrower will use the Loan only for the following purpose: [describe — e.g. purchase of kitchen equipment for the bakery]. Using the Loan for a materially different purpose without Lender’s written consent is a default.

clauses.title: Borrower’s Promises
clauses.rationale: The small set of ongoing promises that keep a private loan administrable: truthful information, reachable borrower, and honesty about trouble before it compounds.
clauses.body: Borrower promises that the information Borrower gave Lender in connection with the Loan is accurate; that Borrower will notify Lender in writing of any change of address; and that Borrower will tell Lender promptly if Borrower expects to be unable to make a payment on time.

clauses.title: Collateral
clauses.rationale: Included when the wizard says the loan is secured. Making the security interest good against third parties usually takes steps beyond the agreement itself (a precise description, and often a public filing); the clause says what the parties agree — perfecting it is a task the rationale flags, not one the template can perform.
clauses.body: As security for the Loan, Borrower grants Lender a security interest in the following property: [describe the collateral precisely]. Until the Loan is repaid in full, Borrower will keep the collateral in good condition and insured against ordinary risks, and will not sell, give away, or further encumber it without Lender’s written consent. When the Loan is repaid in full, Lender will confirm in writing that the security interest is released.

clauses.title: Events of Default
clauses.rationale: A short, closed list. Long default lists in small private loans mostly create accidental defaults.
clauses.body: Each of the following is a default: (a) Borrower misses a payment and does not cure within [10] days after Lender’s written notice; (b) a statement Borrower made to Lender in connection with the Loan was materially false when made; (c) Borrower transfers or further encumbers any collateral without Lender’s written consent.

clauses.title: What Lender May Do on Default
clauses.rationale: Acceleration is the remedy that matters in a private loan; the clause keeps it explicit and keeps single-default forgiveness from becoming permanent waiver.
clauses.body: If a default occurs and is not cured, Lender may declare the entire unpaid principal and accrued interest immediately due, and may exercise the rights the parties have agreed to in this Loan Agreement. Lender’s decision not to act on one default does not give up the right to act on another.

clauses.title: Collection Costs
clauses.rationale: Offered rather than automatic, same reasoning as the note: fee-shifting is an economic choice, and some places read one-way fee clauses as two-way.
clauses.body: If Borrower defaults, Borrower will pay Lender’s reasonable costs of collection, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, to the extent the parties may lawfully agree to them where enforcement occurs.
